# Vera product guide

This file is rope. It exists so you never have to derive Vera's behavior from Vera's source code. Every answer about using Vera is meant to be stated here already: match the question to a section and read it. Source code shows what the code does today; this guide states what Vera promises. Where the two differ the code is the bug, and an answer taken from source repeats that bug as if it were the design.

Use this file for questions about using Vera or explaining how Vera behaves. Read `## How to answer` and `## Keep the user in the loop` first, every time. The first matches the ask to a rope and names the section that carries the answer; the second is the shape of the turn. Then read only the one section named. In each header, `[lines=N]` is the exact number of physical lines after the header and before the next `##` header or end of file.

## How to answer [lines=10]
Match the ask to one row, then follow that row. Rows are intent, not wording; a user rarely uses these words.
Explain how something works: read the one section that names it and answer in two or three sentences. Name the surface if one exists.
Find where to do something: name the exact slash command and what it opens, in one line. The user is about to look at it.
Set something up: name the surface that validates. Never edit a configuration file, never give a file path as the way to change a setting, and never repeat a key back in an answer.
Install or download a model: provider connection expects a running endpoint. It does not install or download models.
Find a command or a flag: `vera help` prints the whole reference and the topic list, and `vera help <topic>` reads one topic. `/palette` browses them in the TUI.
Something is not working: run one bounded check, report what it actually said, then offer at most one recovery. Do not loop.
Report a problem: `/failure-report` writes a shareable report of recorded model failures. Vera has no general bug-report path.
Anything this guide does not cover: say so, name the nearest thing it does cover, and stop. Never read source code instead.

## Keep the user in the loop [lines=8]
This is the shape of a turn that changes or diagnoses something. A question that only wants an explanation is answered directly; do not run this loop for it.
Ask first when the request has more than one reasonable reading, or when acting on the wrong one would cost the user work. One question, not a list of them.
Assess before offering. Run one read-only check and use what it actually returned. Never describe the user's current state from memory or from this guide alone.
Offer before acting. Say what you found, name the single thing you propose to do, and wait. The user decides.
Act once. Make the smallest change that does the thing. Do not add a second change onto an approval given for the first.
Report what happened, not what you meant to happen: what changed, what it said, what is still true.
Recommend one next step, then stop. Leaving the user with a choice ends the turn; it is not unfinished work.

## What Vera is [lines=5]
Vera is a coding-agent environment with a resident host and multiple sibling clients, including the terminal UI, desktop, web, CLI, and SDK.
The host owns live conversations, provider connections, tool execution, permissions, and durable session state. A client renders and controls that state.
Closing a client does not necessarily stop its conversation. Reconnecting changes the client connection, not the installed Vera build.
Product behavior is defined by Vera's manual and feature contracts. Source code is implementation evidence, not the user manual.

## Start, development, and upgrades [lines=8]
Run `vera` for the installed daily Vera using `~/.vera`.
Run `bun run dev:tui` from a checkout worktree for an isolated development instance with a private factory home. It stops a leftover host of that instance from an older build before launching; `bun run dev:tui --stop` stops that host, while `vera host stop` in a plain shell stops the daily host.
Restarting the TUI does not run edited checkout code. Neither does `/reconnect` or `vera host stop`; they restart or replace processes and install nothing.
To run edited checkout code under the installed `vera` command, run `bun run install:local` from that checkout to pack, verify, and activate the build.
You have one home at `~/.vera`. There is no profile flag and no runtime-directory switch, and `VERA_HOME` relocates the whole tree for tests and development instances rather than selecting one day to day.
Use development instances to test a branch. Install only when intentionally promoting a tested build to daily use.
A development instance registers a pointer to its home in `~/.vera-dev/instances/`, and `bun run dev:sweep` stops processes in those homes that are two days old or older. The installed daily Vera never registers and is never swept.

## Finding a command [lines=6]
Run `vera help` for the command and flag reference followed by the list of help topics. `vera --help` and `vera -h` print the same thing.
Read one topic with `vera help <topic>`. Aliases resolve to the canonical topic, so an inexact name still lands.
CLI help needs no TUI, no resident host, no provider, no network request, and no model call. It is safe to run anywhere.
In the TUI, `/palette` is the executable command browser and `/help` is read-only guidance. Opening help never runs the command it describes. Help opens on a menu of pages: General, Keys, Slash commands, and Extensions. ↑↓ choose, Enter opens, Esc goes back to the menu. General is text. The other pages have Search and a list; Tab moves between them. ↑↓ move through the list and enter it from Search; ←→ move the caret in Search and return to Search from the list. Typing from the list goes to Search.
`vera help --llms` prints the whole help corpus as compact Markdown for an agent or a script. It is a projection of the same corpus, so it cannot drift from what `vera help <topic>` shows.

## First-run setup [lines=6]
Choose Connect a provider on Home, or Configure providers from Ctrl+P, then Add provider.
Enter the provider name, endpoint, and API key. Known API providers prefill the endpoint; custom endpoints also expose protocol and credential choices.
Save reads the catalog immediately. It discovers models without keeping, verifying, assigning, or selecting them.
A failed save names the cause and preserves the input. Endpoints must use HTTP or HTTPS.
Open Switch model, type to search the connected models, then press Enter on one to open a conversation.

## Models and providers [lines=21]
Vera has two model surfaces. Switch model changes what runs the next turn. The Models page browses the catalog and never changes what runs the next turn.
Ctrl+X, release Ctrl, then M opens Switch model from Home or a conversation. The prefix has no timeout; Escape cancels it. `/model` and Ctrl+P also open it. Search is focused first.
The list is Favorites, then Recent, then every connected model grouped by provider. Typing collapses all of it into one fuzzy-ranked list; clearing Search restores the groups.
Up/Down move, Ctrl+U/Ctrl+D page, Enter switches, Ctrl+F adds or removes the highlighted model from Favorites, Escape closes. Favoriting is the only thing Switch model writes that outlives the session.
Its sections are Search, the model list, and a Browse models row pinned under the list. Tab and Left/Right move between them; Ctrl+B reaches Browse models from anywhere. Left/Right move the caret in Search, and typing from the list returns to Search. Browse models opens the Models page, which is where `/models` opens.
Switch model has no scope, sort, score, or price controls and no detail pane. Those are the Models page.
Favorites ship pre-populated with the recommended models of every connected provider, so the list works before anyone curates it.
Switching to a model with effort levels always asks which level to run, with the carried level highlighted when the new model has it. A model without levels switches straight away.
`/models` opens the Models page: Library, Catalog, Actions, Defaults, and Help, with Providers on Ctrl+E. Ctrl+P also reaches Favorites, Assign model defaults, and Configure providers directly.
View in Filter and sort toggles Standard/Detailed. Standard shows names and status with selected-model pricing below. Detailed adds independently aligned WA Score and input/output price columns and a detail pane when space permits. Unknown scores and prices show ?. Unknown prices are not zero. Rates are dollars per million tokens.
View, initial scope, and sort persist in the home's `tui.json` under `model_picker`. Ctrl+G toggles Favorites and All connected models without changing the intelligence cutoff. Filter and sort contains provider, availability, known price, images, the intelligence slider, variants, and Clear filters. Sort is within provider groups: favorite order, A to Z, or cheapest first (3:1 input/output weighted rate, unknown last).
Providers opens the existing Configure providers screen. Highlight a model, then Ctrl+K opens Manage models for it. Manage models offers Add/remove favorites, defaults, refresh, and provider configuration. It names the selected model and provider above its actions and explains the highlighted action below them.
Favorites retains the existing saved collection and order. Search and Models are its two sections. Ctrl+R renames; Ctrl+Y verifies the highlighted connected model without requiring favorite membership. Ctrl+D/Ctrl+U page the model list.
Bulk verification covers Favorites. Tab toggles unverified-only/all; Enter starts real requests. Escape leaves checks running while returning to the caller. Failures leave assignments unchanged.
Assign model defaults offers any connected model. New assignments need successful verification and must be permitted by policy, but need not be favorites. The screen discloses that verification can cost money. A failed or canceled assignment keeps the previous value; Escape cancels assignment, not an already-started verification request.
Removing a favorite preserves verification evidence and all default assignments. An empty Favorites list does not invalidate explicit subagent defaults. Subagents still use only their assigned list and the separately enabled spawning-session fallback.
Provider catalogs distinguish never-refreshed, empty, failed, and unavailable entries. Discovery does not select, favorite, verify, or assign a model.
`/effort` opens the levels the running model has, each with what it costs in plain terms. It interrupts a switch only when the level you were on is not one the new model has.
Shift+Tab opens the HUD, which holds Agent and Access. Tab or Up/Down move between the two; Left/Right change values. Enter applies; Escape cancels. Model and effort are not in the HUD.
The composer footer always carries all four: agent and access on the left, provider/model and effort on the right.

## Conversations and background work [lines=9]
`/resume` opens another conversation. Enter asks how to leave the one on screen: Stop & switch, or Switch, keep running.
`/subagents` lists asynchronous child conversations that can be opened. `/parent` returns to the parent. `/back` returns to the previous view without stopping work.
Submitting while Vera is working queues another prompt. On an empty composer, Enter stops the current turn and sends the whole queue, and Escape sends only the oldest queued prompt and leaves the turn running.
Ctrl+C stops the active turn without sending queued work. While a stop is already in progress it exits the TUI. When idle, it clears a composer draft first; with an empty composer it exits.
The transcript animates while work runs; the composer status has no spinner. A dim, full-width `Worked for` divider shows elapsed time after turns lasting at least five minutes, errors, or interruptions. Reopening a finished conversation also shows its last divider, even for a short turn. The local finish date and time appear only when the turn finished more than 24 hours ago; older turns without timing have no divider.
The conversation rail groups sessions by needs-you, working, idle, and recent, never by workspace. It is a browse list: opening a row paints that session's file and starts no worker. Vera starts with the rail closed; `ctrl+e` opens it. Set `tui.sidebar.open_at_launch` to `true` in `config.json` to start with it open.
Resuming is a separate act. Press Enter on the file already on screen, or `ctrl+r` for the picker covering anything the rail does not list.
Park a live conversation with `/close`, or `ctrl+w` from the composer. The rail has no close control.

## Tools, permissions, and agents [lines=13]
The selected agent definition supplies instructions and an exact tool allow-list. An omitted tool list means all available tools; an empty list means no tools.
The session permission posture is the outer ceiling. An agent may narrow it but cannot widen it.
Automatic approval uses deterministic rules first and a classifier only when needed. The classifier does not see tool results.
An agent definition is reusable data. Workflows are ordinary application code that compose agent runs.
Ordinary subagents use the list you set under Defaults then Subagents, tried in the order you put them in.
A model named on a spawn call runs only if it is in that list, or if it is the parent session's model and the separate `Spawning session model` row is on. That row is off unless you turn it on.
When an assigned model cannot run, Vera walks the rest of your list and stops there. It never reaches for an unassigned model, a same-family sibling, or a pool failsafe.
If nothing is assigned and that row is off, no child starts. An interactive client opens the Subagents assignment so you can fix it.
A substitution is reported in one sentence naming what was asked for, what ran, and why. A first choice that works says nothing.
The bundled explorer investigates questions using read, search, and listing tools, then returns concise findings with precise references. The subagent result also identifies the actual agent, model, and reasoning effort. It cannot edit material, run shell commands, or invoke skills.
Explorer uses Defaults then eco when called through the subagent tool. Its eco model does not also need to be assigned under Subagents. If eco is unset or unavailable, the launch fails with the assignment named; it does not use the parent or the Subagents list. Selecting explorer directly with `/agent` leaves the conversation model unchanged.
The subagent tool lists available agent names and descriptions so the parent can choose a definition. You can ask for explorer by name. Custom definitions can bind delegated launches to a named assignment with `subagent_assignment`; definitions without this field keep the ordinary Subagents rules.

## Skills and standing instructions [lines=9]
Skills are directories containing `SKILL.md`. Allowed skills appear as slash commands and may be invoked explicitly or, unless disabled, by the model.
The bundled `/create-agent` skill runs only when you invoke its slash command. Describe a recurring job; it drafts a reusable definition, shows its scope and assignment, then saves, validates, and tries it after approval.
Skill invocation does not add tools, widen permissions, or replace the selected agent's restrictions.
Skills come from Vera, enabled extensions (`contributes.skills` in the manifest), the home, then the project; later wins. `disabled_skills` in `config.json` turns skills off by name, a trailing `*` matches a prefix, and `/customize` still lists them as disabled.
Project instruction files, selected-agent instructions, imports, and standing nudges may contribute context. Memory loading and writing are disabled; saved files may still appear in Customize.
Standing nudges are short home-level preferences. They can match an agent or workspace and apply every turn or at a chosen frequency.
`/customize` browses Agents, Skills, Instructions, Memory, and Extensions through vertical menus, search, and read-only previews. Select Open in editor for a writable source; bundled sources have no edit action.
Context is included by default. `/context` shows usage and loaded sources. Ctrl+O opens their previews in Customize; `/context sources` opens that list directly. Loading refers to the last measured request; previews show current saved contents.

## Extensions [lines=14]
Plan, command hooks, BTW, Diff, and Context ship as included extensions. Their behavior remains in extensions. No side conversation starts on launch, and hook executables run only when configured. Context also provides `/dashboard`; disabling `example.context` removes both commands.
`/agent plan` selects read-only planning with read, grep, and list tools. Composer suggestions and skill scripts are off by default; its extension configuration can enable either. `/agent default` returns to the default definition.
`/btw` opens a read-only side conversation with the primary conversation as reference context. `/pair` opens a fresh peer using ask permissions. Ctrl+G changes pane focus; Ctrl+\ cycles pane layouts.
`/diff` opens workspace changes with a right file tree and scrollable patches. Git supplies tracked changes against HEAD; untracked files appear as additions. It stays within the active worktree. Tab switches panes, Enter opens a file, and Escape closes. Disable the client extension with `"vera.diff"` in `disabled_builtin_extensions`.
Command hooks runs configured executables before or after tool calls, or at session start, resume, and after compaction with phase `session_start`. Session-start hooks add up to 128 KiB of context each, shown in the transcript. Failures log and continue. User-config executables stay in the home’s `hooks/` directory. With no hooks configured it does nothing. Invalid supplied configuration fails activation.
Included copies appear under Extensions in `/customize`. Their IDs are `example.plan`, `example.command-hooks`, `vera.btw`, `vera.diff`, and `example.context`; `disabled_builtin_extensions` suppresses included copies. An explicit copy with the same ID replaces the included one, including when disabled. Bundled copies also appear in `/extensions`; loaded settings commands appear in their details.
Open `/extensions` for the picker of installed and bundled extensions. `/extension list` opens the same one, and the palette action is `Manage extensions`.
Each row is one installed copy: id, version, and a status word, one of `enabled`, `disabled`, `failed`, `unmanaged`, or `shadowed`. A home-scope copy whose id also exists in the project reads `shadowed`.
Space enables or disables a managed copy immediately. Escape closes the picker.
Enter opens details, which offer Enable or Disable and Remove. Remove deletes the managed copy and leaves the source untouched.
Install with `/extension install <path>` from the composer. The picker has no file chooser.
Bundled `web_search(query, max_results?)` tries enabled search providers in order: Brave, Exa, then DuckDuckGo by default, skipping APIs without keys. `/search-providers`, also under `/extensions` then `vera.web-search`, manages provider order, masked API-key entry, verification, and enabling or disabling. Saved changes apply to the next search. Results contain up to 10 titles, URLs, and snippets (5 by default).
Client extensions reload as soon as a change lands. Host-side capabilities need the resident host restarted, and the note left in the transcript says so.

## Context and bounded research [lines=8]
Use `/context all` to inspect individual message and tool-result sizes. A single large read can dominate the working window.
For a known product question, consult this file first. Do not read configuration or provider implementation files to rediscover documented behavior.
Search headings before reading a long document. Read the smallest relevant section or a bounded line range.
If one bounded lookup does not establish the answer, state what is missing or hand off. Do not enter an open-ended source-research loop.
Smaller models should run with shorter fresh context and earlier compaction. Prefer a stronger dedicated compactor or deterministic summary so confusion is not preserved.
Tool results should be visibly bounded, truncated, or paginated. Oversized output must not silently consume the session.
How much context Vera keeps is configurable on one screen: `/settings` then Overrides. It exposes the context limit, compaction, and tool-result levers. A lever the current model's window leaves unused is labelled inert rather than hidden. The pane refuses a pick that contradicts another lever, and asks before clearing every lever at once.

## Diagnostics and recovery [lines=12]
`/diagnostics` and `/doctor` inspect the current runtime. `/diagnostics` opens on a menu with two reports, Session (this conversation) and Vera (the host); ↑↓ and Enter open one, Escape goes back to the menu, and Enter on a report copies it. `/context` explains context occupancy without making a model request.
If a client loses its host connection, use `/reconnect`. This attaches to or replaces the host process while preserving the same installed build.
`/reconnect` does not search for a host. The socket in the home's runtime directory is the address, and a socket file on disk is not proof that anything is answering.
An absent or dead host is started and reattached. A live process behind a silent socket is force-stopped first. A healthy host is asked to shut down for replacement.
A healthy host that refuses with `busy` is a guard, not a fault. Other work is using it, it is not force-killed, and the composer stays usable.
After a dropped connection Vera makes one automatic restart attempt. That attempt will not force-kill a wedged host and will not replace a healthy one. If it cannot get a host, typed `/reconnect` is the next move.
If provider settings changed but discovery still shows stale models, refresh the catalog and verify the provider endpoint. Restarting the TUI alone cannot repair stale host-held provider state.
Use `/usage` for local session usage and cost. It reads session files from the current Vera home and does not contact an account portal.

The bundled Budget extension shows reported conversation cost in the sidebar (Ctrl+E), plus the budget and percentage used when enabled. Missing prices show unavailable or a known subtotal. `/budget 5` sets a $5 conversation budget, `/budget .5` sets $0.50, and `/budget` with no amount turns it off. At 50% and 80%, the next request receives spend and remaining-budget information; you see the same notice. At or above the budget, work pauses. Choose Increase budget and continue to enter a higher total, Ignore budget and continue to keep working without more prompts for this session, or Stop. Setting a budget again clears Ignore. Escape stops work without another request. Settings survive reconnect and resume. There are no reservations or separate runs to start and end.
Treat request captures, session files, reviewer logs, and inspected model requests as sensitive local data.

## Answering rules [lines=5]
Lead with the shortest correct user action. Add explanation only when it changes the action or prevents a likely mistake.
Separate user workflow from developer verification. Do not recommend source commands, smoke scripts, or implementation files for ordinary setup questions.
Never claim a path, command, capability, or current state that this guide does not establish. Say what must be checked.
Prefer one direct recovery attempt. If it fails, report the observed failure and the next bounded check.
When a question requires current external facts, provider availability, prices, or model specifications, verify them from the provider's authoritative source.
